questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests your ability to design an isolated audit pattern with in-cluster API access, RBAC scoping, and security boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped RBAC for fine-grained access control
- In-cluster API access using Secrets and ConfigMaps
- PVC-backed persistent logs and InitContainers for tooling
- NetworkPolicy for egress control to restrict traffic to the collector
- Health checks (readiness/liveness probes) for reliability

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-baseline
  namespace: example
data:
  baseline.json: |
    {"pods": [], "services": []}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-auth
  namespace: example
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: " collector-auth-token"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
  namespace: example
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: audit-agent
  namespace: example
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: audit-agent
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
      containers:
      - name: auditor
        image: your-audit-image:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do audit.sh; sleep 60; done"]
        env:
        - name: COLLECTOR_URL
          value: "http://collector.audit-system.svc.cluster.local:8080"
        - name: AUTH_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: audit-auth
              key: token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
        - name: baseline
          mountPath: /baseline
          readOnly: true
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: audit-logs
      - name: tools
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: baseline
        configMap:
          name: audit-baseline
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: audit-system
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: collector
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **Pros**: Namespace isolation ensures audit agents don't interfere; NetworkPolicy provides security; PVC enables log persistence for compliance
- **Cons**: Each namespace requires separate Deployment (use Operator/Controller to automate); InitContainer adds startup latency; per-namespace RBAC management overhead increases with cluster size

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to compose a small, repeatable namespace-scoped app using InitContainers, volumes, and secret/config data. It also checks understanding of namespace governance via ResourceQuota, LimitRange, and NetworkPolicy.

## Key Concepts

- InitContainer run-before-main-container ensures content is prepared at startup
- EmptyDir volumes for ephemeral assets; ConfigMap/Secret mounted as files
- ResourceQuota and LimitRange to cap per-namespace usage
- Namespace NetworkPolicy to restrict egress to allowed endpoints
- Minimal YAML skeletons and clear trade-offs

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: content-config
data:
  CONTENT_URL: "https://content-api.local/assets"
```

```yaml
# Secret (base64-encoded token)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: content-secret
type: Opaque
data:
  API_TOKEN: <base64-token>
```

```yaml
# Deployment skeleton (2 replicas) with InitContainer and volumes
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: static-content-host
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: fetch-assets
          image: curlimages/curl:7.83.1
          command: ["sh", "-c", "CONTENT_URL=$(cat /config/CONTENT_URL); TOKEN=$(cat /secret/API_TOKEN); curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer '$TOKEN $CONTENT_URL -o /assets/index.html"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: assets
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
            - name: config
              mountPath: /config
            - name: secret
              mountPath: /secret
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80
          volumeMounts:
            - name: assets
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
      volumes:
        - name: assets
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: content-config
        - name: secret
          secret:
            secretName: content-secret
```

```yaml
# Service
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: static-content-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: static-content-host
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 80
      protocol: TCP
  type: ClusterIP
```

```yaml
# ResourceQuota (namespace-wide)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: ns-quota
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4"
    requests.memory: 8Gi
    limits.cpu: "8"
    limits.memory: 16Gi
    pods: "10"
```

```yaml
# LimitRange (default limits)
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: ns-limits
spec:
  limits:
    - max:
        cpu: "2"
        memory: 2Gi
      min:
        cpu: "100m"
        memory: 128Mi
      default:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 512Mi
      defaultRequest:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 128Mi
      type: Container
```

```yaml
# NetworkPolicy (egress only to content API)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-to-content-api
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - ipBlock:
            cidr: 203.0.113.0/24
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle updates to CONTENT_URL or API_TOKEN without downtime?
- What are the trade-offs of using InitContainer vs a sidecar for content updates?

````yaml
      - name: app

````

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: CronJobs, Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and RBAC in a single cohesive workflow. Emphasizes idempotence, cleanup, and rollback in a real maintenance task.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and Job lifecycle
- ConfigMap and Secret integration
- PersistentVolumeClaim mounts
- ServiceAccount with RoleBinding
- ttlSecondsAfterFinished and history limits
- Observability: logs and data integrity

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: daily-archive
  namespace: data-archive
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: archive-sa
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          volumes:
            - name: data
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: data-pvc
            - name: archive
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: archive-pvc
          containers:
            - name: archiver
              image: myorg/archive-tool:latest
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              envFrom:
                - configMapRef:
                    name: archive-config
                - secretRef:
                    name: archive-creds
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data
                  mountPath: /data
                - name: archive
                  mountPath: /archive
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "archive --older-than ${ARCHIVE_DAYS} --src /data --dst /archive"]
              resources:
                requests:
                  cpu: "100m"
                  memory: "128Mi"
                limits:
                  cpu: "500m"
                  memory: "512Mi"
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test idempotency if ARCHIVE_DAYS changes while a run is mid-flight?
- What monitoring would you add to alert on failed archives and ensure timely rollback?

## Why This Is Asked
Auditors assess knowledge of Kubernetes pod security hardening and defense-in-depth strategies.

## Key Concepts
- Pod securityContext vs container securityContext
- runAsNonRoot enforcement and UID requirements
- readOnlyRootFilesystem and volume mount implications
- Capability dropping and privilege escalation controls
- Seccomp profiles via annotations and runtime defaults
- Rolling update safety and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
# Security hardening patch for collector Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: collector
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod: runtime/default
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000
        fsGroup: 2000
      containers:
      - name: collector
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - ALL
          volumeMounts:
          - name: input
            mountPath: /data/input
          - name: output
            mountPath: /data/output
        # Preserve existing probes and resources
        # livenessProbe, readinessProbe, resources remain unchanged
```

## Validation & Rollback
**Validation:**
- `kubectl get pods -n apps -l app=collector -o yaml | grep securityContext`
- `kubectl auth can-i create pods --as=system:serviceaccount:apps:collector`
- Test pod startup and volume access
- Verify non-root execution: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- id`

**Rollback:**
- `kubectl rollout undo deployment/collector -n apps`
- Monitor rollout status: `kubectl rollout status deployment/collector -n apps`
- Document security context changes in version control

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question assesses practical CKAD competencies including PersistentVolumes, InitContainers, Jobs/CronJobs, Secrets, NetworkPolicies, and observability—skills essential for production Kubernetes workloads.

## Key Concepts

- **PVC mounting and volume permissions**: Namespace-scoped storage with appropriate access modes
- **InitContainer tooling**: Pre-installing dependencies (curl) without inflating the main container image
- **Job scheduling and idempotency**: CronJobs running every 5 minutes with collision prevention
- **NetworkPolicy egress controls**: Restricting traffic to least-privilege access patterns
- **Secret management**: Secure credential handling via Kubernetes Secrets
- **Health probes**: Ensuring application availability and reliability through readiness and liveness checks

## Common Pitfalls

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates CKAD competencies in CronJob scheduling, InitContainers for tooling bootstrap, PVC-mounted database operations, health probes, lifecycle hooks, and rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- **CronJob**: Scheduled jobs using cron syntax (0 2 * * * for daily at 02:00)
- **InitContainer**: Bootstrap tool installation (sqlite3) before main container runs
- **SQLite Operations**: DELETE with WHERE clause for date filtering, VACUUM for storage reclamation
- **Probes**: readinessProbe and livenessProbe on /healthz endpoint
- **Lifecycle Hooks**: preStop sleep for graceful shutdown
- **PodDisruptionBudget**: minAvailable: 1 ensures availability during disruptions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: log-pruner
  namespace: ckad-practices
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: log-pruner
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache sqlite"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: db
              mountPath: /data
          containers:
          - name: pruner
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "sqlite3 /data/logs.db 'DELETE FROM logs WHERE created_at < date(\"now\", \"-30 days\"); VACUUM;'; curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"deleted\":\"$(date)\"}' http://ops-portal:8080/api/v1/prune-summary"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: db
              mountPath: /data
            resources:
              requests:
                memory: "64Mi"
                cpu: "100m"
              limits:
                memory: "128Mi"
                cpu: "500m"
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
            lifecycle:
              preStop:
                exec:
                  command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
          volumes:
          - name: db
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: log-pruner-pdb
  namespace: ckad-practices
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-pruner
```

## Rollback Strategy
Maintain version-controlled YAML manifests in a Git repository. On failure, execute:
```bash
kubectl apply -f log-pruner.yaml --record
kubectl rollout undo cronjob/log-pruner
```
Alternatively, use a GitOps tool like ArgoCD or Flux for automated rollbacks.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of the sidecar pattern for config reloading without full pod restarts.

## Key Concepts
- Sidecar container pattern
- inotify for file system monitoring
- SIGHUP for process signal handling
- ConfigMap mounting and reload behavior
- Zero-downtime configuration updates

## Patch Example
```yaml
# payments/processor-deployment.yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: config-watcher
          image: busybox:stable
          command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - |
              apk add --no-cache inotify-tools
              inotifywait -m -e modify -r /etc/processor |
              while read path event; do
                kill -HUP 1
              done
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 65534
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/processor
              readOnly: true
```

## Verification Under Load
1. Apply patch and verify pod rollout: `kubectl rollout status deployment/processor -n payments`
2. Simulate ConfigMap update: `kubectl create configmap processor-config --from-literal=data=updated --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`
3. Verify sidecar detects change: `kubectl logs processor-<pod> -c config-watcher -n payments`
4. Confirm main process reloads: check application logs for reload indicators
5. Load test with tools like `hey` or `wrk` to verify zero downtime during reload

## Rollback Procedure
1. `kubectl rollout undo deployment/processor -n payments`
2. Verify previous version: `kubectl rollout status deployment/processor -n payments`
3. Confirm stable state: `kubectl get pods -n payments -l app=processor`

Why This Is Asked
- Validates CKAD basics: Jobs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, probes in a practical data-migrate flow.
- Introduces idempotence with a marker, a common real-world concern.

Key Concepts
- Job lifecycle and completion guarantees
- InitContainer usage for tooling installation
- Runtime config from ConfigMaps and Secrets
- PVC-based idempotence markers and backoff settings
- Probes and minimal YAML scaffolding

Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Job skeleton (pseudo)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: data-migrate
spec:
  backoffLimit: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: csvkit-install
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache python3 py3-pip && pip3 install csvkit"]
      containers:
      - name: migrator
        image: curlimages/curl:7.88.0
        command: ["sh", "-c", "python3 migrate.py"]
        env:
        - name: MIG_BATCH_SIZE
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: mig-config
              key: MIG_BATCH_SIZE
        - name: API_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: mig-creds
              key: api-token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data/migrate
        - name: marker
          mountPath: /data/marker
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: migrate-pvc
      - name: marker
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: migrate-marker-pvc
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      # probes would be defined on the migrator container
```

Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle partial CSV failures and ensure exactly-once semantics?
